priority.override_reason: Ranks 1 through 4 are closed by the 2026-07-27 frame-stack, direct-eval, and constructor fast-gate evidence; ranks 5, 7 through 13 have fresh profiles identifying distinct direct-call, typed-loop, parser, numeric, or array/property costs. Rank 6 and rank 14 both spend material time in the same RegExp matcher path, specifically match_pattern_first scanning quantified simple atoms through an allocated boundary vector. This unit reduces that shared matcher cost without source-path, workload-name, checksum, or iteration-count admission.

mechanism.summary: Stream eligible non-Unicode single-code-unit quantified RegExp atom candidates directly into match_pattern_first, preserving greedy or lazy backtracking order without allocating a boundary vector for every quantified atom.
mechanism.generality: Eligibility is derived solely from immutable parsed RegExp pattern state and matcher options. It applies to every non-Unicode simple atom repetition with no atom capture, regardless of script source, benchmark identity, input length, or result. Unicode and multi-code-unit atoms, captured atoms, and all unsupported patterns retain the existing boundary-vector matcher.
semantic_risks: preserving ECMAScript greedy and lazy candidate priority when a continuation backtracks
preserving captures owned by surrounding groups while excluding only atoms with direct capture effects
falling back for Unicode, surrogate-pair, zero-width, and multi-code-unit atom semantics
preserving RegExp test, exec, replace, and stateful lastIndex behavior through the unchanged result protocol
